newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Libya's Gaddafi hopes for new Clinton.
newsitem.headline: Libya's Gaddafi hopes for new Clinton.

text.p: Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi on Wednesday expressed hope that re-elected U.S. President Bill Clinton will now show himself as he really is, free from the need to court popularity.

Gaddafi said Clinton's win ..."brings nothing new. The world knows him and has lived with him for four entirely futile years, with his failed projects and the blood of the children of Lebanon, Bosnia, Iraq, Somalia, Rwanda and Liberia flowed in torrents."

"What is new is that in the next four years Clinton will act as he really is after ridding himself of the various pressures - especially the Zionist pressure, and the need for hypocrisy and political compliments, to win votes.
"Today Clinton is responsible before his conscience alone and for the first time the world will know Clinton the real man," said the statement from the official Libyan news agency JANA.
U.S. presidents can only serve two terms in office.
The United States has a long list of grievances against Libya, including its refusal to surrender two Libyan nationals accused of blowing up Pan Am Flight 103 over Lockerbie, Scotland in 1988.
The attack killed 259 people aboard the plane and 11 people on the ground.
Libya has since 1992 been under United Nations sanctions, including an air and arms embargo, over the Lockerbie case, and the United States imposed economic sanctions on it more than 10 years ago.
Clinton in August signed a law aimed at preventing new foreign investment in Libya and Iran, two countries which Washington believes back "international terrorism".

"Whole peoples from Libya to Yugoslavia, Somalia, Iraq, Sudan, Cuba, Palestine and Iran were besieged. Clinton's friends in Egypt, Syria, the Gulf and North Africa found themselves under siege, intentionally or not, because of these stupid policies of interference in which Clinton was involved or he inherited," the statement added.
